extraction_notes.note: Equation (14) writes the diffusion coefficient as $\nu$ but the following sentence calls it $\delta>0$, and (15) uses $\delta$; kept verbatim.

The cited monotonicity of the condition number in $\varepsilon$ (cf. FZ07) shares one sentence with the root-finding definition, so it stays inside the algorithm step rather than a separate external theorem.
Convergence orders are read off log-log error plots (figures only); recorded as numerical claims attached to the experiment examples.

Discussion-only paragraphs (cost of shape optimization, stable algorithms LLHF, future work in Section 8, figure/table captions) and applied cited tools (Reverse Cuthill-McKee, BDF4, SBDF2, BICGSTAB) get no nodes.

nodes.statement: Of these, the so-called intrinsic methods attempt to solve PDEs using surface-based meshes and coordinates intrinsic to the surface under consideration; this approach can be efficient since the dimension of the discretization is restricted to the dimension of the surface under consideration (e.g.).

nodes.statement: Let mathcal P denote the projection operator that takes an arbitrary vector field in R^3 at a point x=(x,y,z) on the surface and projects it onto the tangent plane to the surface at x.
nodes.raw_latex:
Let ${ \mathcal P}$ denote the projection operator that takes an arbitrary vector field in $\mathbb{R}^3$ at a point
$\mathbf{x}=(x,y,z)$ on the surface and projects it onto the tangent
plane to the surface at $\mathbf{x}$.
nodes.clean_text: Let mathcal P denote the projection operator that takes an arbitrary vector field in R^3 at a point x=(x,y,z) on the surface and projects it onto the tangent plane to the surface at x.

nodes.statement: Letting n=(n^x,n^y, n^z) denote the unit normal vector to the surface at x, this operator is given by mathcal P = mathcal I - nn^T = (1 - n^x n^x) & -n^x n^y & -n^x n^z \\ -n^x n^y & (1 - n^y n^y) & -n^y n^z \\ -n^x n^z & -n^y n^z & (1-n^z n^z) = p^x & p^y & p^z , where mathcal I is the 3-by-3 identity matrix, and p^x, p^y and p^z are vectors representing the projection operators in the x, y and z directions, respectively.
nodes.raw_latex:
Letting $\mathbf{n}=(n^x,n^y, n^z)$ denote
the \emph{unit} normal vector to the surface at $\mathbf{x}$, this
operator is given by

\begin{align}
{ \mathcal P} = { \mathcal I} - \mathbf{n}\mathbf{n}^{T} =
\begin{bmatrix}
(1 - n^x n^x) & -n^x n^y & -n^x n^z  \\
-n^x n^y & (1 - n^y n^y) & -n^y n^z \\
-n^x n^z & -n^y n^z & (1-n^z n^z) 
\end{bmatrix} =
\begin{bmatrix}
\mathbf{p}^x & 
\mathbf{p}^y &
\mathbf{p}^z 
\end{bmatrix},
\label{eq:proj_mat}
\end{align}

where ${ \mathcal I}$ is the $3$-by-$3$ identity matrix, and $\mathbf{p}^x$, $\mathbf{p}^y$ and $\mathbf{p}^z$
are vectors representing the projection operators in the $x$, $y$ and $z$
directions, respectively.
